Senses.Explanation: The side position is the differentiated member of Caodong positional language: it is where forms, speech, and responsive activity are located in contrast with the straight position. Caoshan Benji identifies it with the realm in which myriad forms appear, then turns that classification into an interview test when a monk claims to come from the side position. Linquan Conglun preserves the refusal in his appraisal. Yongjue Yuanxian classifies merit and royal-son sequences as matters on this side while warning against mechanically mapping separate schemes together. Baiyu and Dahui Zonggao both expose a limit: diagrams and verbal explanations can themselves remain side-position talk. The term therefore names a relational position inside these attested schemes; it is not a general synonym for error, inferiority, or one physical side.

ModifierControls.Finding: The translation keeps a named position and does not turn the modifier into a free-standing judgment that something is wrong.

FamilyControls.Finding: The straight position is the explicit contrasting member and must remain separately searchable.
The side within the straight names a compound relation, not the bare side position.
The straight within the side reverses that compound relation.
The five positions provide one recurrent system in which the headword is deployed, but the system name is not its gloss.
